On either, onError clears the runner's page alert and reloads the version; a 409 sets the 'changed, re-apply' banner and a stale 422 sets FormAlert's error, which is cleared at the next submit. Any other refusal returns early and keeps the draft. FormAlert renders p4ProblemMessage, which is translated by code from the catalogue and React-escaped, never the server detail; the 422's errors[] carries only a pointer and a generic message, so no hidden literal is in it. The server raises restricted_token_stale only in updateVersion (versions.ts:815, after the If-Match check at :811). On a rule create, resolveRestrictedTokens(null) refuses every marker as restricted_marker_unknown before the retired-form check (versions.ts:505), so the new text, which names 'the rule editor', can only appear in the editor's PATCH flow. The only web consumer is RulePage.tsx:426. The new en text is accurate. The ar text is provisional and carries the same meaning. ADR-0051 part B now matches the code. The web still only tests the token marker pattern (ContentEditor.tsx:48, for the restricted label) and never computes a tag. No secret-like literal was added. Nothing in the diff touches authorization, concurrency, audit or I/O.

B: PATCH 409, banner shown, stale text absent; re-apply 200 with S kept. C1 (other rule's [restricted:<tag>:1]), C2 ([restricted:3:1]) and C3 (the rule's own tag from row version 2) all get 422 with If-Match "3".
